hello.note: More formal: selamat sejahtera. Between Muslims: assalamualaikum (reply: waalaikumussalam).

goodbye.note: Said by the one leaving. The one staying behind says selamat jalan.

please.note: Asks someone to do something. Sila invites them: sila duduk (please sit). To ask for a thing: minta …

thank_you.note: Thank you very much: terima kasih banyak.

no.note: Casual: tak. To say 'not' before a noun or pronoun, use bukan: bukan saya (not me).

excuse_me.note: Used before asking a stranger something. To get past someone: tumpang lalu.

how_are_you.note: Also works as a general greeting, like hello.

whats_your_name.note: To a woman: siapa nama cik? (puan if she is older or married). Anda works for anyone but sounds formal.

where_from.note: To a woman: cik (or puan) berasal dari mana? Casual: asal dari mana?

speak_english.note: Politer with a title first: encik boleh cakap … (cik to a woman).

speak_slowly.note: Sikit is the everyday form of sedikit (a little).

where.note: Casual: kat mana? or just mana?

what.note: Apa dia? sounds softer when you didn't catch what was said.

where_bathroom.note: Bilik air (washroom) is also common. Casual: tandas kat mana?

what_time.note: Answer with pukul + number: pukul tiga (three o'clock).

one.note: Before a counter word it becomes se-: seorang (one person), sebuah (one thing).

eight.note: Indonesian says delapan; in Malaysia it is lapan.

ten.note: Eleven is sebelas, twenty is dua puluh.

water.note: Order plain water as air kosong, or ais kosong for iced water. Pronounced ah-eer.

coffee.note: Kopi comes with condensed milk; kopi O is black with sugar.

tea.note: Teh tarik is frothy 'pulled' milk tea; teh O is without milk.

bill_please.note: At a casual stall people often just say kira! (add it up).

no_meat.note: Daging often means red meat only; add ayam pun tak (no chicken either) to be clear.

enjoy_meal.note: A host inviting you to start: jemput makan.

airport.note: In everyday speech many people simply say airport.

hotel.note: Same word as in English, said ho-tel with even stress.

train_station.note: Kereta alone means car. For city rail: stesen LRT or stesen MRT.

want_to_go.note: In everyday speech: saya nak pergi ke …

one_ticket.note: With a destination: minta satu tiket ke …

cheaper.note: To bargain: boleh kurang sikit? (can you lower it a bit?)

id_like_this.note: Also saya ambil yang ini (I'll take this one).

cash.note: To pay in cash: bayar tunai. Many people just say cash.

yesterday.note: Semalam can also mean last night.

good_evening.note: Used from mid-afternoon until dusk. After dark, greet with selamat malam.

good_night.note: Also a greeting after dark. Right before bed: selamat tidur.

see_you_later.note: If you'll meet again the same day: jumpa nanti.

call_police.note: The emergency number in Malaysia is 999.

need_doctor.note: Also saya perlu jumpa doktor (I need to see a doctor).

dont_feel_well.note: Kurang sihat is the polite, usual way to say it. Casual: tak sihat.

hospital.note: Same word as in English. For minor problems, look for a klinik.

allergic.note: Example: saya alah kepada kacang (nuts). Many people also say saya alergik …

be_careful.note: Also jaga-jaga! Warning signs say awas.

no_problem.note: Tak apa (it's fine, never mind) is also very common.

maybe.note: Casual speech often adds kot at the end of a sentence instead.
